title: A half-size French Violin, circa 1910, bearing the label Breton Brevette. The one-piece back, ribs and scroll showing some narrow figure, the table of open broad grain narrowing to the right flanks, the transparent varnish of a golden-orange colour

A seven-eighth size Markneukirchen Violin, circa 1920, bearing a label with initials G P & S. The two-piece back of medium flame descending from the joint, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of narrow grain widening on the flanks, the transparent varnish of a golden-yellow colour

A small size Bavarian Violin, circa 1900. L.O.B. 12⅝in. (322mm.). The two-piece back of faint figure, the ribs and scroll plain, the table of open broad grain, the varnish of a red-brown colour on a yellow ground

A Violin by G. HARTMANN in Mainz, bearing a manuscript label dated 1908. L.O.B. 14⅛in. (359mm.). The one-piece back of narrow curl, the ribs of similar curl, the scroll plain, the table of medium grain, the varnish of an orange red-brown colour. Minus tailpiece. Temporary fingerboard

A three-quarter size Violin by Francois Barzoni, bearing the maker's label Fecit anno 1900, Manufacture Speciale de la Maison Beare et Fils a Londres with a brand F.B on the button and bottom rib. L.O.B. 13¼in. (337mm.), in shaped case. The two-piece back of narrow flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of broad grain, the transparent varnish of a red-brown colour

A small size German Violin, circa 1900. L.O.B. 12⅝in. (320mm.), with a bow in case. The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of medium grain narrowing to the right flanks, the varnish of an orange-red-brown colour

A Violin by H. CLOTELLE in Mirecourt, circa 1920. L.O.B. 14⅛in. (359mm.). The two-piece back of narrow flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of narrow grain, the transparent varnish of a red colour

A Mirecourt Violin, circa 1920, labelled JEAN BAPTISTE VUILLAUME. L.O.B. 14⅛in. (359mm.). The two-piece back, ribs and scroll of narrow figure, the table of broad grain, the varnish of a clear red colour. (Minus tailpiece, bridge)

A Violin by Thibouville Lamy Mirecourt, circa 1920, labelled THIERRY A PARIS. L.O.B. 14⅛in. (359mm.). The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of medium grain, the varnish of a red-brown colour. (Minus tailpiece and top nut)

A Markneukirchen Violin, circa 1910, labelled Maggini. L.O.B. 14¼in. (362mm.). The one-piece back and ribs of bird's-eye figure, the scroll of narrow curl, the table of medium grain, the varnish of a clear red-brown colour on a yellow ground

A Violin, circa 1880, labelled GENNARO FABRICATORE ANNO 1809 Napoli. L.O.B. 13⅞in. (352mm.). The one-piece back, cut on the slab showing narrow curl, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of narrow grain, the varnish of an orange-brown colour on a yellow ground

A Violin by DONALD B. A. PALMER, bearing the maker's label with initials. Fecit in Cremona 1977 No. 34. L.O.B. 14in. (356mm.), in case. The one-piece back, cut on the slab showing convoluted grain, the ribs and scroll of medium curl, the table of close grain, the transparent varnish of a light-orange colour

A Viola by David Dix, bearing the maker's label in Southwark, London, circa 1980. L.O.B. 16⅜in. (415mm.). The two-piece back of narrow flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of strong medium grain, the varnish of a red colour on a yellow ground

A good German Violin, circa 1890. L.O.B. 14⅛in. (359mm.), with a bow in case. The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of narrow grain widening to the flanks, the varnish of a red colour on a light brown ground

A good French Violin, circa 1830, attributed to Francois Breton. L.O.B. 14³/₁₆in. (359mm.), in case. The one-piece back of narrow curl and root figure ascending to the right, the ribs of medium curl, the scroll plain, the table of strong narrow grain widening slightly on the left flanks, the transparent varnish of a golden-amber colour. Excellent condition

A French Violin of the Barzoni School, circa 1900. L.O.B. 14³/₁₆in. (362mm.), with a Dresden School bow, the frog of mother-o'-pearl, in case. The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of narrow grain widening to the flanks, the transparent varnish of an orange-brown colour

A good French Violin of the Laberte-Humbert School, circa 1890. L.O.B. 14⅛in. (359mm.), with a silver-mounted bow, in shaped leather case. The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of medium grain, the clear varnish of a golden-brown colour

A fine Violin by EDWARD WITHERS, bearing the maker's label at 22 Wardour Street, London, dated 1888. L.O.B. 14³/₁₆in. (362mm.), in shaped case. The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs of similar curl, the scroll of medium curl, the table of narrow grain, the clear oil varnish of a golden-orange colour. Excellent condition. This maker a reputed pupil of Jack Lott

A good French Violin by Charles DROUIN, bearing the label: Lutherie Artistique, Mirecourt 1895, No. 432. L.O.B. 14⅛in. (359mm.), in a shaped polished walnut wood case. The two-piece back of broad flame descending from the joint, the ribs and scroll of medium curl, the table of narrow grain widening to medium on the flanks, the clear varnish of a red-brown colour on a yellow ground

A Violin by J. Brown, stamped J. BROWN maker probably James Brown in Spitalfields, London, circa 1830. L.O.B. 14³/₁₆in. (365mm.), in case. The two-piece back of narrow flame ascending from the joint, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of narrow grain, the varnish of a clear brown colour

A Violin by EMILE LAINE bearing the maker's label: Luthier. Bruxelles, dated 1927. L.O.B. 14¼in. (362mm.). The one-piece back of narrow curl, the ribs and scroll of similar faint curl, the table of medium grain, the oil varnish opaque thick red colour on a yellow ground

A Violin by ERNEST REINHOLD, bearing a label in Saxony, circa 1890. L.O.B. 14³/₁₆in. (360mm.). The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of narrow grain widening to broad, the clear varnish of a brown colour

A good Violin by HARRY DOBBS, bearing the maker's label in Sutton Coldfield, dated 1971, No. 28. L.O.B. 14in. (356mm.), in case. The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of narrow grain, the transparent varnish of a golden-yellow colour

A Viola by William Robinson, bearing the maker's label in Plumstead, London, dated 1925. L.O.B. 16¼in. (413mm.), in case. The one-piece back of medium curl ascending to the right, the ribs and scroll of less figure, the table of narrow grain, the oil varnish of a red colour on a yellow ground. With a pamphlet by William Robinson on 'My Craft and Myself'

A good Violin bearing the label of EVASIO EMILIO GUERRA fece in Torino ANNO 1927. L.O.B. 14in. (356mm.), in case. The one-piece back of medium to broad curl, the ribs and scroll of similar figure, the table of strong narrow grain, the clear varnish of a red-brown colour on a yellow ground

An English Violin, circa 1820, of the Betts School. L.O.B. 14in. (356mm.), in case. The one-piece back, cut on the slab showing small figure on the left flanks, the ribs of narrow curl, the scroll plain, the table of strong medium grain, the varnish of a brown colour on a yellow ground

A Markneukirchen Violin, circa 1910, labelled Paul Bailly. L.O.B. 14¼in. (362mm.), in case. The two-piece back of narrow flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of narrow grain widening to broad on the flanks, the varnish of a red colour on a yellow ground

A Viola attributed to JOHANN ANDREAS HAMM in Klingenthal, circa 1760. L.O.B. 15³/₁₆in. (385mm.), in case. The one-piece back of faint narrow curl, the ribs and scroll plain, the table of narrow grain, the varnish of a brown colour

A French Violin, circa 1880, of the CHIPOT VUILLAUME School. L.O.B. 14⅛in. (359mm.), in case. The two-piece back of narrow flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of narrow grain, the transparent varnish of a red brown colour

A Violin by Alexander SMILLIE, bearing the maker's label: ALEX SMILLIE at Crosshill, Glasgow, 1894. L.O.B. 14⅛in. (359mm.). The one-piece back of broad curl ascending to the right, the ribs of similar curl, the scroll of medium figure, the table of narrow grain, the clear varnish of a red-brown colour on a yellow ground

A Violin by George PYNE, bearing the maker's label in London, dated 1910, and branded G. PYNE, LONDON, on the centre inner back. L.O.B. 14in. (356mm.), in shaped Hill case with cover. The two-piece back of narrow flame, the ribs and scroll of similar figure, the table of medium grain, the varnish of a light brown colour

A Viola, circa 1880, bearing the label CHARLES BOULLANGIER fecit London 1883. L.O.B. 15¹³/₁₆in. (398mm.), in a shaped brown leather case lined purple velvet. The two-piece back of medium flame ascending from the joint, the ribs and scroll of medium curl, the table of medium grain widening on the flanks, the varnish of a rich red-brown colour. (Two holes bored in back of pegbox and a small hole in bottom rib)

A Violin by CLAUDE AUGUSTIN MIREMONT in Paris, circa 1850, with the receipt of Messrs. W. E. Hill and Sons, London, dated April 1959. L.O.B. 14in. (356mm.). The two-piece back of medium flame descending from the joint, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of even broad grain, the oil varnish of a red-brown colour on a yellow ground craquelled. Condition good

A rare Violin by FRANCISCUS MARIA PUPUNATUS, bearing the maker's label Fecit Lausannae, dated ANNO 1837. L.O.B. 14⅛in. (360mm.). The one-piece back of medium curl, the ribs of similar curl, the scroll of narrow curl, the table of strong narrow grain, the varnish of a light red-brown/colour on a yellow ground. Fine condition

A good Violin by Ernest & Paul VOIGT, circa 1946, bearing a label E. & P. VOIGT. L.O.B. 13⅞in. (353mm.), in case. The one-piece back of medium curl, the ribs similar figure, the scroll of faint curl, the table of narrow grain widening on the flanks, the clear varnish of a red-brown colour on a yellow ground

A Violin attributed to Josef Johann RAUCH in Komotau Bohemia, circa 1770, bearing a label NICOLAUS AMATUS. L.O.B. 13¹⁵/₁₆in. (355mm.), in a polished shaped wood case. The two-piece back showing broad figure, the ribs of varied narrow curl with bird's-eye figure, the scroll of narrow curl, the table of narrow grain, the varnish of a red-brown colour on a yellow ground. Overall condition good

A Viola by LABERTE-HUMBERT FRERES in Mirecourt, circa 1890. L.O.B. 15⅞in. (404mm.), in shaped case. The two-piece back of medium flame descending from the joint, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of narrow grain widening to medium on the flanks, the transparent varnish of an orange-red colour on a yellow ground

A Violin, circa 1900, of the George Withers School. L.O.B. 14³/₁₆in. (362mm.), in a rosewood veneer case. The two-piece back of good narrow flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of medium grain, the varnish of an orange colour on a yellow ground

A Violin, circa 1870, probably Austrian, bearing a label Jo BETTS, No. 2 NEAR NORTHGATE, THE ROYAL EXCHANGE, LONDON, 1792. L.O.B. 14⅛in. (359mm.), with two bows (one silver mounted) in case. The two-piece back of medium flame descending from the joint, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of medium grain, the varnish of a brown colour

A Violin by James Hardie & Son, bearing the maker's label in Edinburgh, dated 1881. L.O.B. 14³/₁₆in. (362mm.), with two bows in case. The two-piece back of faint medium flame, the ribs and scroll of similar figure, the table of medium grain, the varnish of a thick deep red colour

A good Violin by Wolff Bros. in Kreuznach, dated 1889, No. 567. L.O.B. 14⅛in. (359mm.), with two bows in case. The two-piece back of narrow flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of narrow grain, the varnish of an orange-brown colour on a golden-amber ground

A Mirecourt Violin, circa 1930. L.O.B. 14⅛in. (359mm.). The one-piece back and ribs of bird's-eye figure, the scroll of narrow curl, the table of medium grain, the transparent varnish of a golden-brown colour. Minus tailpiece

A Violin by BRETON BREVETE in Mirecourt, circa 1900, bearing the maker's signed label and branded Breton on the fingerboard. L.O.B. 14¹/₁₆in. (357mm.). The two-piece back of narrow flame, the ribs and scroll plain, the table of narrow grain, the transparent varnish of a golden-amber colour. Minus tailpiece

A Mirecourt Violin, circa 1930, labelled P. BEUSCHER LUTHIER A PARIS. L.O.B. 14⅛in. (359mm.). The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll plain, the table of narrow grain widening to the flanks, the transparent varnish of an orange-red colour. Minus tailpiece

A small size Mirecourt Violin, circa 1930, labelled Copie Breton Brevete and branded on the button. L.O.B. 13¼in. (338mm.). The two-piece back, ribs and scroll of narrow figure, the table of medium grain, the transparent varnish of a red-brown colour on a yellow ground. Minus tailpiece

A German Violin, circa 1880, of the Lowendall Berlin School. L.O.B. 14³/₁₆in. (362mm.), with a bow by HERMANN FIELDER, DRESDEN, stamped on the shaft. With shaped case. The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of medium grain widening to broad on the flanks, the varnish of a transparent red colour on a brown-yellow ground

A Saxon Violin by Hawkes & Son, London, dated 1930. The Tyrolese Violin. L.O.B. 14⅛in. (359mm.), with a silver mounted bow in shaped case. The two-piece back of narrow flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of narrow grain, the varnish of a transparent red colour

A Violin by VON DOLLING (Junior) in Markneukirchen, circa 1910, bearing the manuscript label. L.O.B. 14⅛in. (359mm.), in case. The handsome two-piece back of medium flame descending from the joint, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of narrow grain, the transparent varnish of a brilliant light orange colour

A Violin by Frank R. KNIGHT, bearing the maker's label in Reigate, Surrey, dated 1918. Pupil of W. GLENNISTER. L.O.B. 14⅛in. (359mm.), in case. The two-piece back of narrow flame, the ribs of similar curl, the scroll plain, the table of narrow grain widening to the flanks, the varnish of a red colour on a yellow ground

A Saxon Violin, circa 1920, by Hawkes & Sons, London, bearing their label Tyrolese Violin. L.O.B. 14⅛in. (359mm.), in case. The two-piece back of narrow flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of close grain, the transparent varnish of a red-brown colour

A Viola by Andreas Kreuzinger (JNR.), bearing the maker's label: Geigenmacher Mittenwald, dated 1977. L.O.B. 16¹/₁₆in. (410mm.), in shaped case. The two-piece back of narrow flame, the ribs of similar curl, the scroll of medium curl, the table of narrow grain widening to the flanks, the varnish of a red-brown colour on a yellow ground

A Violin by Enrico Rossi, bearing the maker's label: FABRICATORE DI INSTRUMENTE (PIAZZA DELIA TRINTA?) N 464 IN PAVIA, dated 1866. L.O.B. 14in. (356mm.), in double case (case poor condition). The two-piece back of medium flame descending from the joint, the ribs and scroll of narrow curl, the table of medium grain, the oil varnish thick and craquelled of an orange-brown colour on a yellow ground. (A small chip off corner lower left table, otherwise excellent condition)

An interesting Violin, circa 1850, bearing the label: ANTONIO GIBERTINI DI PARMA PREMIATO PIU VOLTE IN MILANO CON MEDAGLIA ETC. PEL RISTABILIMENTO DELLA CELEBRE SCUOLA Cremonese Fecit anno 18(52?). L.O.B. 14in. (356mm.), in case. The two-piece back cut partly on the slab showing curl ascending from the joint, the ribs with diagonal curl the scroll of faint figure, the table of even medium grain, the varnish of a very transparent yellow colour. (The table in fair condition)

A good French Violin bearing the label of V. J. Charotte, Luthier Paris. D'APRES STRADIVARIUS, MEDAILLE ARGENT EXP BRUXELLES 1897. MEDAILLE d'Or EXP. 1900. L.O.B. 14in. (356mm.). The two-piece back of broad flame descending from the joint, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of medium grain, the varnish of a red colour on a yellow ground. Imitation graft and minor repairs

An English Violin, circa 1840, of the Furber School. L.O.B. 14¼in. (362mm.). The two-piece back showing broad mottled figure, the ribs of similar wood, the scroll of narrow curl, the table of even broad grain, the transparent varnish of a golden-yellow colour, the flanks on the back showing red colour. Minus tailpiece and fingerboard top nut

A Klingenthal School Violin, circa 1820, branded below the button WRONNER BERLIN and labelled Carolus Antonius Tanegia. L.O.B. 13⅞in. (352mm.), with three bows (one silver mounted), in case. The one-piece back and ribs of narrow curl, the scroll plain, the table of medium and narrow grain, the varnish of a brown colour on a yellow ground

A good Violin by Ferdinand PATZELT, in Dresden, bearing the maker's brand on the inner back dated 1910. L.O.B. 14⅛in. (359mm.), in a walnut veneer case. The two-piece back of medium flame descending from the joint, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of strong narrow grain, the varnish of a red-brown colour on a light brown ground. This maker achieved first prize at Bologna

A good Violin by Paul VOIGT, bearing the maker's label in Oxford Road, Manchester, dated 1906. L.O.B. 14³/₁₆in. (360mm.), in a shaped brown leather crocodile grain leather case, lined green plush. The one-piece back of medium curl sloping to the left, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of fine grain widening to the flanks, the soft oil varnish of a deep red-brown colour. In an excellent state of preservation

A fine Violin by Charles BOULLANGIER, bearing the maker's label: Fecit London and dated 1883. L.O.B. 14¹/₁₆in. (357mm.), with two bows (one seven-eighth size), in shaped case with waterproof cover. The one-piece back of handsome medium curl ascending to the right, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of medium grain, the varnish of a red-brown colour. With the certificate of Messrs. J. & A. Beare, London, dated April 1953. Stating it is in an excellent state of preservation

A fine Violin by Bela SZEPESSY, bearing the maker's label Szepessy Bela, dated London 1889, L.O.B. 14⅛in. (359mm.), in case. The handsome two-piece back of medium flame descending from the joint, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of medium grain, the oil varnish very lightly craquelled, of a clear orange-red colour on a gold yellow ground. Fine condition. See Illustration, Plate I

A silver and tortoiseshell mounted Violin Bow by W. E. Hill & Sons stamped W. E. Hill & Sons on the shaft. The tortoiseshell frog with pearl eye and ring, the octagonal stick with silver face of a red-brown colour. 57 grams. Minus lapping

A fine Violin by Joseph Rocca, bearing the maker's label: JOSEPH ROCCA fecit PREMIATO DI MEDAGLIE ALLE ESPOSIZIONE DE TORINO, GENOVA, LONDRA E PARIGI TAURINI. Anno Domini 1857. I.H.S. and branded G.R. on lower blocks. Length of back 14in. (356mm.), in shaped black wood case. The two-piece back of handsome medium flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of strong medium grain, the clear varnish of a golden-brown colour. With the Certificate of Messrs. W. E. Hill & Sons dated London February 1920, stating a characteristic example with original label and handsome figured wood etc. See Colour Illustration, Plate II and Catalogue Covers

A fine Viola by Antonio CAPELA. Antense. Espino, Portugal, bearing the maker's signed label Faciebat Anno 1972. Length of back 16½in. (420mm.), in shaped lined case. The two-piece back of fine quality narrow flame, the ribs and scroll of similar figure, the table of broad grain, the clear varnish of a golden-orange colour
A good gold mounted Viola Bow by GARNER WILSON stamped on the shaft. The tortoiseshell frog with double gold ring inset the sides, the round stick with gold face, of a red-brown colour. 73 grams

A fine Violin by Antonio Capela, bearing the maker's signed label in Antense, Espino, Portugal, dated Anno 1971. L.O.B. 13¹⁵/₁₆in. (354mm.), in case. The two-piece back of narrow flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of strong medium grain, the clear varnish of a golden-amber colour. Mint condition

A Violin by Richard Duke in London, circa 1760, branded below the button DUKE, LONDON. L.O.B. 13¹⁵/₁₆in. (355mm.), in case. The one-piece back of horizontal narrow curl, the ribs of similar curl, the scroll plain, the table of medium grain, the varnish of a brown colour. Overall condition excellent. See Illustration, Plate III

A Violin, circa 1800, of the John Betts School. L.O.B. 13⅞in. (353mm.), in case. The one-piece back of medium to broad curl, the ribs of similar less figure, the scroll of narrow curl, the table of strong narrow grain widening to the flanks, the varnish of a clear brown colour on a light brown ground. With the certificate of Joseph A. CHANOT in London, July 1898, stating the violin sold this day was made by Vincenzo PANORMO

A good Violin, circa 1840, bearing the label Joseph GUARNERIUS fecit Cremone anno 1738. L.O.B. 13¾in. (350mm.), with a silver mounted bow in an oblong black cloth covered case with cover. The two-piece back of broad flame, the ribs and scroll of medium curl, the table of broad grain narrowing to the flanks, the varnish of a brown-red colour on a light brown ground. With the receipt of Messrs. J. & A. Beare, London, dated February 1965 for a Violin copy of Joseph GUARNERIUS DEL GESU ascribed to Joseph Fendt, circa 1840
A silver mounted Violin Bow by H. KRETZSCHMANN stamped on the shaft. The ebony frog with plain sides, the octagonal stick of a red-brown colour. 60 grams

A Viola bearing the label JANUARIUS GAGLIANO FILIUS ALEXANDRI FECIT NEAP 17. With the certificate of Joseph Vedral, s'Gravenhage July 1948, stating: We guarantee that the viola of Gagliano, Naples sold by us, is Italian, all parts are genuine and belong together. Length of back 15⁹/₁₆in. (395mm.), with shaped case lined brown plush and waterproof cover. The two-piece back almost plain, the ribs of narrow curl, the scroll plain, the table of strong medium grain widening to open broad grain on the flanks, the varnish of a brown colour on a light brown ground

A fine Violin by Joseph ALBANI in Botzen first quarter 18th Century, bearing the label JACOBUS STAINER IN ABSOM PROPE OENIPONTUM 1653. Length of back 13¹⁵/₁₆in. (355mm.), with a silver mounted bow stamped TOURTE on the shaft in case. The two-piece back of narrow flame ascending slightly from the joint, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of narrow grain, the varnish of a clear red-brown colour. With a letter of Messrs. W. E. Hill & Sons, dated London May 1932, stating: the Violin is the work of Joseph Albani. Etc and I suppose there is no doubt the violin came from Giardini the player. See Illustration, Plate IV

A silver mounted Violin Bow by EUGENE NICOLAS SARTORY A PARIS stamped in two places on the shaft. The ebony frog with rounded heel, the sides with pearl eye and ring (minus one pearl eye), the round stick of a red-brown colour (minus lapping). 59 grams. The brass eye in the frog has created a small chip off the shaft mortice

A Violin by GIOVANNI GRANCINO in Milan, CIRCA 1690, bearing part of the label only. Length of back 14in. (356mm.), in an oblong case with cover. The two-piece back of narrow curl, cut partly on the slab, the ribs of broader curl, the table of medium grain widening slightly to the flanks, the varnish of a red-brown colour on a yellow ground. Condition fair with some over polish. With the Certificate of MESSRS. W. E. Hill & Sons, dated London November 1924. See Illustration, Plate V

An interesting Violin, 18th Century. Length of back 13¹⁵/₁₆in. (354mm.), upper bouts 6⅜in. (162mm.), lower bouts 8in. (204mm.), in a shaped blackwood case with cover. The two-piece back of narrow figure, the ribs similar, the scroll cheeked, plain, the table of strong even narrow grain, the varnish of a clear brown colour, the middle back with a light over varnish of a red colour. Overall condition excellent

A Violin by Joseph GAGLIANO in Naples, with a letter of Messrs. W. E. Hill & Sons in London, dated May 1913, stating: 'The instrument (with the exception of the head, which is English, the work of Norris & Barnes) was made by Joseph Gagliano of Naples about 1770-1780. It is a fair example of the maker's work". Length of back 14in. (355mm.). The two-piece back of medium flame ascending from the joint, the ribs of similar curl, the scroll of medium curl, the table of narrow even grain, the varnish of a golden-brown colour. The violin bears the remains of a Nicolo Amati label. See Illustration, Plate VI

A Violin by Joannes Baptista Guadagnini, bearing the maker's label: CREMONENSIS FECIT TAURINI ALUMNUS ANTONI STRADIVARI 1778 and initials G.B.G over T. Length of back 13¹⁵/₁₆in. (355mm.), in a shaped oblong black leather case with cover. The two-piece back showing handsome mottled curl figure, the ribs and scroll of medium curl, the table of narrow grain widening to medium broad on the flanks, the varnish of a clear brown colour on a yellow ground. The instrument has had a fair amount of restoration in the past but is in excellent playing order. See Colour Illustration, Plate VII

A Violin by HANNIBAL FAGNOLA, bearing the maker's label: Fecit TAURINI ANNO DOMINI 1913 with monogram and in manuscript, 'COPIA DI' above a second label JOANNES FRANCISCUS PRESSENDA q RAPHAEL fecit TAURINI anno DOMINI 1848. A signature can just be seen on the upper left rib. Length of back 14¹/₁₆in. (357mm.). The two-piece back of medium flame descending sharply from the joint, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of even medium grain, the clear varnish of an orange-red colour on a yellow ground. With a copy of receipt from Sydney Evans Ltd., dated October 1978. See Illustration, Plate VIII
A fine Bow Box by W. E. Hill & Sons, London. Of mahogany with ebony stringing surrounds. The interior lined pink floral brocade. Brass fittings. To take four Violin or Viola Bows

A fine Bow Box by W. E. Hill & Sons, London. Of wood, possibly stained walnut with ebony stringing surrounds. The interior lined green grass colour velvet. To take four Violin or Viola Bows. Brass fittings
A fine Bow Box. Of oak with ebony stringing. The interior lined green velvet. To take two Violoncello Bows
A silver mounted Viola Bow by W. E. Hill & Sons, stamped W. E. Hill & Sons on the shaft. The ebony frog with pearl eye and ring, the round stick with silver face of a red-brown colour. 69 grams

A silver mounted Violin Bow by W. E. Hill & Sons, stamped W. E. Hill & Sons on the shaft. The ebony frog with silver shields inset the sides, the octagonal stick with silver face of a red-brown colour. 58 grams
A fine Violin Bow by W. E. Hill & Sons, stamped W. E. Hill & Sons on the shaft. The ebony frog with pearl eye and ring, the octagonal stick with silver face of a red-brown colour. 58 grams
